name: MonarchGauge
title: Gauge
summary: A half-circle meter for one reading against a scale, built on the SwiftUI Gauge: bands give the scale a meaning, a target is marked, and the value is written as text.
whenToUse: For one reading that people judge against a range: utilisation, a health score, a quota used.
whenNotToUse: For progress towards completion, use ProgressView. For several quotas, use MonarchUsageMeter. For a value over time, use MonarchSparkline. In a tight row, the system Gauge styles (accessoryCircular, linearCapacity) are smaller.
api: MonarchGauge.init(_ label: String? = nil, value: Double?, in range: ClosedRange<Double> = 0...100, description: String? = nil, bands: [MonarchGaugeBand] = [], target: Double? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil, indicator: MonarchGaugeIndicator = .arc, size: MonarchGaugeSize = .md, noValueLabel: String? = nil, valueLabel: String? = nil, showsRange: Bool = true, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil)
MonarchGaugeBand.init(_ range: ClosedRange<Double>, tone: MonarchTone, label: String? = nil)

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label under the gauge and its spoken name. "Gauge" is spoken without one.

options.name: value
options.description: The reading. nil shows an empty track and a dash.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: bands
options.description: Stretches of the scale with a tone and a name.

options.name: target
options.description: A target on the scale, marked with a tick and added to the spoken value.

options.name: tone
options.description: The colour of the value arc. nil takes the tone of the value's band, or the accent without bands.

options.name: indicator
options.description: arc fills the track to the value; needle draws the bands on the track and points at the value.

options.name: size
options.description: sm (120), md (160) or lg (200) points wide at most.

options.name: noValueLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text "No data".

options.name: showsRange
options.description: Writes the ends of the scale under the arc.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes every number. The default is a number in the current locale.

states.name: with a value
states.description: The track is filled to the value (arc) or a needle points at it; the value is written in or under the dial.

states.name: in a band
states.description: The arc takes the band's colour and the band's name is written under the value.

states.name: no value
states.description: An empty track, a dash, and "No data" as the spoken value.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Drawn at the nearest end of the scale; the text shows the real value.

appearance: A muted track; the value arc in the accent colour, or the solid colour of its band's tone. Bands use the solid tone colours, and the strong border colour for neutral. The tick and the needle use the default text colour, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web draws its own SVG and exposes a meter role; here the control is a SwiftUI Gauge with an internal GaugeStyle, and the spoken value is set explicitly because a custom gauge style does not carry one. The web size is a number of pixels and the thickness can be set; here there are three sizes and the thickness is 12% of the width. The web tones include accent; here nil is the accent and the other tones are MonarchTone. The scale starts at the leading end, so the dial and its range are mirrored in right-to-left layouts; the web one is not. At accessibility text sizes, and with a needle, the value is written under the dial instead of inside it. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The gauge is one element. Its label is the given label, or "Gauge".
The value is the reading and the name of its band ("72, At risk"), or the reading and the range ("72 (from 0 to 100)"), followed by the target ("Target 80").
Without a value it reads "No data".
The value and the band name are written as text, so the reading does not depend on the arc or its colour.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; the dial keeps its size, and at accessibility sizes the value moves under it so it is never clipped.
The change of the arc and the needle is animated, and not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A range whose ends are equal is widened by one.
A value that is not finite is treated as no value.
A value exactly on the boundary of two bands belongs to the upper one.
A band without a label falls back to the range in the spoken value; give every band a label.
Bands that reach beyond the range are drawn up to its end.

examples.title: With bands
examples.template:
MonarchGauge(
    {{label}},
    value: {{value|double}},
    description: {{description}},
    bands: [
        MonarchGaugeBand({{bands.0.from|double}}...{{bands.0.to|double}}, tone: {{bands.0.tone|tone}}, label: {{bands.0.label}}),
        MonarchGaugeBand({{bands.1.from|double}}...{{bands.1.to|double}}, tone: {{bands.1.tone|tone}}, label: {{bands.1.label}}),
        MonarchGaugeBand({{bands.2.from|double}}...{{bands.2.to|double}}, tone: {{bands.2.tone|tone}}, label: {{bands.2.label}}),
    ],
    formatValue: { "\(Int($0.rounded()))%" }
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: {{locale}}))
examples.code:
MonarchGauge(
    "CPU load",
    value: 76.0,
    description: "Average over 5 minutes",
    bands: [
        MonarchGaugeBand(0.0...70.0, tone: .success, label: "Healthy"),
        MonarchGaugeBand(70.0...90.0, tone: .warning, label: "High"),
        MonarchGaugeBand(90.0...100.0, tone: .danger, label: "Critical"),
    ],
    formatValue: { "\(Int($0.rounded()))%" }
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-US"))

examples.title: A ratio written as a percentage
examples.code: MonarchGauge("Quota used", value: 0.55, in: 0...1, size: .sm, formatValue: { $0.formatted(.percent) })

examples.title: A needle
examples.code:
MonarchGauge(
    "Score",
    value: 40,
    bands: [
        MonarchGaugeBand(0...50, tone: .danger, label: "Low"),
        MonarchGaugeBand(50...100, tone: .success, label: "Good"),
    ],
    indicator: .needle
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web formats the value with an Intl.NumberFormat option bag (unit percent, no decimals); the native gauge takes a formatValue closure, so the template writes the same text (76%) with a closure.
parityExceptions.convention: Locale-driven formatting is native: Swift and Kotlin format numbers in code, not with Intl options.
